description: Somos TerraShield, un equipo multidiciplinario que une tecnologia,datos y creatividad para comprender nuestro planeta. En el NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 buscamos transformar datos satelitales en informacion util para identificar tendencias ambientales y apoyar la prevencion ante lluvias extremas, inundaciones y huaicos. Nos interesa la programacion, IA, desarrollo web, GIS, visualizacion de datos y diseño.
summary:
EarthShift is a web-based Earth observation analytics platform (React + Python) designed to uncover hidden climate and ecological anomalies before they escalate into environmental or agricultural crises. Using Piura, Peru as a pilot region, EarthShift harmonizes 26 years (2000–2026) of NASA satellite datasets—including MODIS Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2), MODIS Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1), GPM Precipitation (GPM_3IMERGM), and GLDAS Soil Moisture (GLDAS_NOAH025_M)—across both regional and micro-zone scales (ValleChira, BajoPiura, BosqueSecoMorropon, and DesiertoSechura).
Through three analytical engines—Earth Paradox, Silent Collapse, and Decision Reversal—the system detects subtle divergences between moisture, thermal stress, and vegetation health that traditional monitoring misses. By translating complex NASA Earth science data into transparent, actionable early-warning insights without fabricating missing observations, EarthShift empowers farmers, researchers, and local authorities to shift from reactive disaster response to proactive, data-driven prevention.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

EarthShift is an interactive Earth observation intelligence platform designed to uncover hidden climate and ecological anomalies before they escalate into visible environmental or agricultural disasters. Using Piura, Peru as a high-vulnerability pilot region, our pipeline ingests, cleans, and harmonizes 26 years (2000–2026) of multi-sensor NASA satellite observations into a standardized monthly time series (region_id, date, variable) across both regional (piura_general_01) and micro-zone scales (ValleChira, BajoPiura, BosqueSecoMorropon, and DesiertoSechura).

Instead of analyzing single variables in isolation, EarthShift feeds harmonized Land Surface Temperature (MOD11A2.061), Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1.061 NDVI/EVI), Precipitation (GPM_3IMERGM), and Soil Moisture (GLDAS_NOAH025_M v2.1) into three specialized analytical engines:

  • Earth Paradox: Identifies counterintuitive divergences between hydrological inputs (rainfall/soil moisture) and thermal or biophysical responses.
  • Silent Collapse: Detects gradual, multi-month vegetation and moisture degradation that precedes acute drought or ecosystem stress.
  • Decision Reversal: Highlights thresholds where historical assumptions fail, signaling decision-makers to pivot agricultural or water-management strategies early.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional climate monitoring often reacts only after crop failure, severe drought, or flooding is already visible. EarthShift bridges the gap between raw NASA remote sensing archives and actionable local governance. By offering micro-zone granularity alongside regional context, it enables farmers, water managers, and local authorities in northern Peru to anticipate water stress, optimize irrigation planning, and protect vulnerable dry-forest and coastal-valley ecosystems.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Data Engineering & Scientific Processing: Python (pandas, numpy, scipy) for quality filtering, cloud masking, spatial bounding-box aggregation, and temporal harmonization.
  • NASA Data Access Platforms: NASA AppEEARS (MODIS products) and NASA Giovanni (GPM & GLDAS time-series extraction).
  • Backend & API: Python (FastAPI / REST architecture) serving processed anomaly indicators and geospatial payloads.
  • Frontend & Visualization: React, interactive geospatial mapping, and time-series dashboards.

Creativity & Scientific Factors Considered

Our team prioritized strict scientific integrity and data traceability over artificial gap-filling:

  • No Fabricated Observations: We established a core scientific rule never to interpolate or invent missing satellite observations, explicitly distinguishing between missing data, low-quality pixels, and true absence of anomalies.
  • Methodological Rigor (MOD16 Exclusion): During data auditing, we identified that NASA's MODIS Evapotranspiration (MOD16A2GF.061) systematically outputs fill value 32762 (Barren or sparsely vegetated land-cover mask) across Piura's hyper-arid coastal zones and the Sechura Desert. Rather than introducing bias, we documented this exclusion and reconstructed the surface water-energy balance by combining GPM precipitation, GLDAS soil moisture, MODIS LST, and NDVI/EVI.
